name: Foundations First: differentiated learning (Teaching at the Right Level) (Ambitious Impact, 2025 idea report)
summary: Ambitious Impact's 2025 estimate for a new charity scaling up Teaching at the Right Level (grouping primary pupils by learning level rather than grade), counting the higher lifetime earnings that better test scores bring. The idea Foundations First was founded to run (AIM's 2026 cohort). The sheet models the Philippines (costs, income, fertility); the charity works in Kenya, where costs and incomes are lower, so the figure is AIM's for the idea, not for the charity's country. A re-implementation of AIM's spreadsheet, traced from its final cost per income doubling ($45; the report's range is $12–45).

rows.explainer:
e.g. DALYs / count / % reduction / etc Using lower end estimate from most cited study on the income effects of improved test scores: 1 SD improvement in test scores leads to a 10-45% income increase. Consistent with approach used in the SP report. https://docs.google.com/document/d/18v_i5NLxG5QSQIfNm3ADmcT5qEuJEeY6R4N0Eq9ilN4/edit?tab=t.0

Range from the report (§6.2): 1 SD of test scores raises income by 10–45% in the literature; AIM takes the low end.

rows.label: % teacher-led programs
rows.explainer:
It is unclear to us (Mix and Filip) which model we should assume the charity would deliver. Volunteer-led models are up to 3x more effective, but their feasibility may depend on the local context of the target country. We're using a 50/50 split. Future users should pick whichever value is most appropriate for their program/their target country.

Range ours: from AIM's 50/50 split to all teacher-led (the less effective model, which governments more often run).

rows.label: Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Default for programs where staff deliver the help themselves (treatment, counselling, coaching, outreach): staff pay is about half the cost. Our judgment; we haven't seen this program's breakdown.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Health workers and field staff at nonprofits often earn somewhat less than in comparable jobs. Our judgment.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff per dollar of cost (in-kind donation)
Share of the full cost paid in cash
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Ambitious Impact counts income in years of doubled consumption. A doubling for a year is ln 2 of log-consumption, which is one GiveWell unit of value at the shared value of income, so the result ranks with the GiveWell models. With credit by share of resources, times the share of the full cost paid in cash (staff's forgone pay is the rest).
